blocks.title: DevOps
blocks.text: DevOps is a set of practices that combines software development (Dev) and IT operations (Ops) to improve collaboration, efficiency and agility in delivering software products and services (Fig. 1.6). Its main goal is to shorten the development lifecycle, improve software quality and provide continuous delivery with high reliability.

items: Improved collaboration: a culture of collaboration between development and operations teams breaks down silos and aligns them on common goals.
Faster time-to-market: automation with continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) delivers updates and new features more rapidly.
Enhanced quality: continuous testing and monitoring find and fix issues early.
Increased efficiency: automating repetitive tasks reduces manual effort and human error.

blocks.text: DevOps is ideal for web and mobile apps and cloud services where fast development and scaling are crucial; for example, Amazon's e-commerce platform uses DevOps to release new features and updates continuously. It may be less suitable for highly regulated or hardware-dependent projects; software for medical devices, for instance, needs rigorous testing and compliance that may not fit DevOps's rapid pace.

blocks.prompt: Which of these is not a benefit of DevOps: improved collaboration, enhanced quality, increased project scope creep, faster time-to-market (MCQ 6)?
blocks.explanation: Increased project scope creep, option (c): scope creep, the uncontrolled growth of a project's scope, is a problem, not a benefit. The book's answer key gives (b), which is listed in the text as a benefit.

items: DevOps: development plus IT operations; shorter lifecycle, better quality, continuous delivery (Fig. 1.6).
Benefits: collaboration, faster time-to-market (CI/CD), quality, efficiency; suits web, mobile and cloud (Amazon), less so regulated or hardware-dependent projects.
